description: We are a student team interested in software development, web technologies, data analysis, and space science. We aim to build an innovative, functional solution using NASA data and modern technologies. We welcome teammates interested in coding, UI/UX design, data visualization, research, and scientific storytelling.
summary:
Lunar Echo is an interactive digital archive that brings the forgotten stories of NASA's space missions and abandoned space technology back to life.

Inspired by the NASA Space Apps Challenge theme "Abandoned but not Forgotten," our project explores historical spacecraft, scientific instruments and mission hardware that continued to contribute to science even after their missions ended.

Our featured story highlights the Apollo 13 S-IVB lunar impact and the Apollo 12 seismic experiment, demonstrating how a discarded rocket stage created vibrations that helped scientists study the Moon.

Through interactive mission stories, timelines, visual explanations and historical references, Lunar Echo makes space history easier to discover and understand.

Our vision is to preserve these forgotten stories and inspire future generations to explore the history of space exploration.
details: Lunar Echo is an educational digital archive that preserves and presents the stories of forgotten space technology and historical NASA missions. Our project explores how spacecraft, scientific instruments and mission hardware continue to have scientific and historical importance even after their missions end. One of our featured stories is the Apollo 13 S-IVB impact experiment. In April 1970, the discarded Saturn V third stage was directed to impact the Moon. The Apollo 12 Passive Seismic Experiment recorded the resulting lunar vibrations, helping scientists study the Moon's internal structure. Our platform presents historical mission information, timelines, seismic explanations, interactive visual elements and references in an accessible format. The project uses web technologies and a structured database approach to organise information and make space history easier to explore. Our goal is to preserve these stories, support space education and make forgotten space technology accessible to future generations.
